description: Provision of immigration clearance facilities in the voluntary repatriation of persons, who left the country during the war period without using an approved port and a valid passport and have been granted asylum in India and have confirmed their Sri Lankan identity
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-08-10 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body:
- Persons who left the country without using an authorized port of departure or possessing a valid passport for entry into India due to the instability that prevailed in the country during the war period, were subsequently displaced and registered as refugees with the Government of India and are now anticipating voluntary repatriation through the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR). Advices of the Attorney General have been received regarding the provision of required immigration clearance facilities for repatriating them. While taking measures as per the instructions given by the Attorney General, Cabinet approved the proposal made by the Minister of Public Security and Parliamentary Affairs to make provisions for repatriating Sri Lankans who have left the country:

Obtaining a clearance report from the State Intelligence Service regarding persons who left the country before 2006-08-01 without using an authorized port of departure or possessing a valid passport and are displaced in India and have verified their identity as Sri Lankans through the Sri Lankan Overseas Missions in that country.


Verifying that they have not committed murder, treason and other offences specifically provided for or prescribed by law.


To issue temporary passports to the relevant persons and to allow them to enter the country through an approved port without taking any legal action in accordance with the Immigrants and Emigrants Act, No.20 of 1948.


To allow Sri Lankans who had illegally migrated to India within the period from 2006-08-01 to 2009-05-19, the date on which the war ended, without using an authorized port of departure or possessing a valid passport and have obtained a clearance report from the State Intelligence Service after verifying their identity, to enter the country through an approved port without being subject to any legal action under the Immigrants and Emigrants Act, No.20 of 1948, in accordance with the powers vested in the Controller General of Immigration and Emigration.


If there are persons who are liable for murder, treason and offenses for which special provisions are made or must be prescribed by law, they will be detained at the port and referred to the relevant institutions for further legal action.
